text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
QADISSIYA
- More world condemnation of Turkish invasion of northern Iraq.
- Turkish demonstrators burn U.S. flag in Ankara.
- Iraq and Yemen review bilateral relations.
- UAE newspaper calls for Arab coordination to face challenges confronting Arab nation.
- British magazine urges Labour Party to reconsider policy towards Iraq.
- Arab League issues fresh condemnation of Turkish invasion of northern Iraq.
- Vice-president receives Bulgarian diplomat.
- Polish companies express readiness to provide Iraq with medical supplies.
- Egypt signs oil deals with Arab and foreign companies.
- Izzat Ibrahim, vice-chairman of Revolutionary Command Council, heads meeting on next census to be conducted late this year.
(The above were also carried by JUMHOURIYA and AL-THAWRA)
- Article says U.S. isolation due to its tough Iraq policy increases and European countries show more understanding towards Baghdad.
JUMHOURIYA
- Article says water will be challenge Arabs have to face in 21st Century.
- Article says Pentagon will not be able to control world in 21st Century.
- Work continues on Badoush dam in northern Iraq.
THAWRA
- Italian parliamentary delegation, visiting Iraq, says Italian MPs will work hard to have Iraq's frozen assets in their country released.
- Commentary on new challenges facing Iraq due to presence of Turkish troops in its north.
- Article on link between oil and Arabs' national security.
- Article on President Saddam Hussein's guidelines for just world economic order.
